extracted.intended_audience: KDD 2026 Research-track reviewers and prospective research-track authors (machine learning / data science community)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and reviewer requirements for Research Track submissions to KDD 2026: criteria authors should meet and reviewers should apply when assessing submissions across novelty, technical quality, impact, reproducibility, ethics, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical merit / technical quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical merit (Technical Quality): Reviewers assess the soundness of methodology, rigor of experiments, and validity of conclusions. Submissions should demonstrate strong execution and robust reproducibility practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate soundness of methods, experimental rigor, whether conclusions follow from results, and whether execution is strong. Consider robustness and reproducibility practices (e.g., experimental design, statistical rigor, ablations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty/Originality: Papers must present innovative contributions. The CFP explicitly welcomes "visionary papers on new and emerging topics" and emphasizes that work should avoid being merely comprehensive surveys without novel intellectual contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the contribution is new and non-trivial relative to prior work; prefer clear novel ideas or perspectives rather than only comprehensive summaries. Reward visionary or emerging-topic contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impact / impact potential
rubrics_metrics.description: A range of factors including ... potential impact. Additional Consideration: Impact potential — The significance and applicability of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge significance, breadth of applicability, potential to influence research or practice, and whether results open useful new directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of execution (part of primary criteria): refers to how well the work is carried out and validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessment of experimental thoroughness, implementation care, appropriate baselines, reproducible protocols, and whether claims are supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of presentation / Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity: Papers must be well-written and clearly presented in English, following ACM formatting standards. The first 8 pages should be self-contained since reviewers aren't obligated to read beyond that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate organization, readability, clarity of figures and tables, correctness of English, adherence to ACM format, and whether the core contribution and results are fully viewable within the first 8 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related work / positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Related work: Proper positioning within existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether authors cite and compare to relevant prior work, clearly explain distinctions and contributions relative to existing methods, and avoid missing key references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility: Code, data availability, and methodological transparency. Primary evaluation listed reproducibility of results as a factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer submissions that provide code and data or clear instructions to reproduce experiments; assess transparency of methods, parameter settings, seeds, and evaluation protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations / Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical considerations: Responsible data use and informed consent where applicable. Ethics is explicitly listed as a factor for decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether data collection and usage respect privacy and consent, consider potential harms, include ethical risk discussion/mitigations, and follow applicable norms and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and self-contained first 8 pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must follow ACM formatting standards and the first 8 pages should be self-contained since reviewers aren't obligated to read beyond that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure main contributions, methods, and results appear within first 8 pages; supplementary material may be used for appendices but reviewers may ignore content beyond page 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer subject-matter expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate reviewers should have demonstrated subject matter expertise, with at least three papers in KDD (Research or ADS track) or similar machine-learning, AI or data science conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area Chairs should select reviewers who meet this bar; reviewers are expected to have prior publication experience in relevant venues indicating expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process involves at least three independent reviewers overseen by an Area Chair, providing comprehensive evaluation across these dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each submission receives at least three independent reviews and that Area Chairs coordinate and moderate reviewer discussion and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct and review completeness enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If any author of a submission who is also a reviewer does not carry out the reviewing task properly, no author of that submission will see the reviews during rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural enforcement to ensure reviewers who are also authors perform reviews properly; reviewers should complete reviews fully and on time to avoid sanctions affecting their own submission's rebuttal visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI disclosure in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Any use of generative AI tools during the reviewing process must be disclosed in the review form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly state in the review form if they used generative AI tools (e.g., for drafting text or summarization); Area Chairs and organizers may use disclosures to assess review provenance and integrity.
